caveats.summary: How restricted each fund's money is comes from this site's reading of the city's fund descriptions.
caveats.text: How tightly a fund's money is restricted is this site's reading of the Description of Funds (Budget Book pp. 258-261), not a figure the city printed. Each fund shows the sentence it was read from. "unknown" means those pages do not say; it is a reading, not a gap.

caveats.summary: A department here is not the division of the same name elsewhere; don't add them.
caveats.text: Budget Book pp.85-125 print two blocks per page: spending by DIVISION above, and each DEPARTMENT's funding sources below. Five names are both a department and a division beneath it: City Council, City Manager, City Attorney, General Services and Administrative Services. A mark here is the whole department across every fund; a mark of the same name on the General Fund's breakdown is one division of it.

caveats.summary: What a fund pays departments is not what it takes in; two different pages print them.
caveats.text: What a fund takes in is printed on Budget Book pp.127-140; what departments draw from it is printed on pp.85-125. They are two pages, not one figure read twice, and either may be the larger.

caveats.summary: The FY2023-24 actual and FY2024-25 revised columns are checked only department by department.
caveats.text: Budget Book pp.66-67 print citywide totals for the two adopted years only, so the actual and revised columns here are checked against each department's own printed total and nothing citywide. Five of the eleven departments miss that total by exactly one dollar, all in the FY2023-24 actual column; the mapping declares each as the city's own rounding.

caveats.summary: These rows say what a division spends, not which fund pays for it.
caveats.text: The upper block of Budget Book pp.85-125 prints what each division spends by category, whatever fund pays for it, so no row here has a fund. The fund breakdown is the lower block of the same pages, drawn as its own chart, and it is by department, not division, so the two cannot be joined. A division here has no fund group, and a chart coloured by group leaves it grey.

caveats.summary: Each ribbon here is a cell of one printed table, not money moving from one box to another.
caveats.text: These pages print one table: divisions down, spending categories across. A chart can read it either way round, and neither is money moving, so every ribbon here says so. Adding up a whole column gives that column's printed total and nothing more.

caveats.summary: Spending here is all counted as outside the city, including charges between departments.
caveats.text: Elsewhere on this site, spending is outside money or a charge between departments according to the fund group it comes from. These rows name no fund group, so every ribbon is published as outside money, and Internal Service Fund charges are inside these figures. Don't add a figure from here to an outside-money total from another page.

caveats.summary: How restricted each fund's money is comes from this site's reading of the city's fund descriptions.
caveats.text: How tightly a fund's money is restricted is this site's reading of the Description of Funds (Budget Book pp. 258-261), not a figure the city printed. Each fund shows the sentence it was read from. "unknown" means those pages do not say; it is a reading, not a gap.

caveats.summary: Revenue the charts draw is the same money the Over time page prints; don't add the two.
caveats.text: Budget Book pp.127-140 appear in two places on this site: the charts draw one adopted year at a time, and the Over time page prints all four columns (FY2023-24 actual, FY2024-25 revised, and both adopted years). A row found in both is one printed figure shown twice.

caveats.summary: Click into any part of the citywide chart and the pages it opens into add back up to it, to the cent.
caveats.text: Each part of the citywide chart opens into the finer pages of the budget book that break it down: revenue lines (pp.127-140), funds, General Fund divisions (pp.167-170), spending categories (pp.167-183) or departments (pp.85-125), transfers (p76 and p222) and fund balances (pp.186-209). Added up, they equal the citywide figures on pp.66-67. A box marked derived holds money a page prints for a group and no finer page breaks down.

caveats.summary: In this file an opened box repeats its members' links, so adding every link counts money twice.
caveats.text: An opened node draws a link to each of its members. The General Fund's link to each division totals the rows drawn beyond it; every other node's repeats each link arriving at the member, or leaving it where the node takes nothing in, with the same figure and facts. A remainder cites the members it is the difference of. So 220 printed figures sit behind more than one link, and summing every value_cents in this file counts them more than once.

caveats.summary: A revenue line marked "one row" is how Budget Book pp.127-140 print that whole category.
caveats.text: Some funds' revenue in a category is one row named for the category, such as Charges for Services. Where a fund prints no other row of that category, this site labels the line "<category>, one row": pp.127-140 print it as a single row for its category, so nothing is missing from it.

caveats.summary: Some fund groups carry money that no single fund's own page prints.
caveats.text: Budget Book pp.66-67 print each fund group's change in balance as one figure. Where some of a group's funds draw on their balances and others add to them, that figure is the net of the funds' changes, which no single fund carries, so for 3 fund groups each group's net is drawn on a box of its own. A fund of such a group is drawn with what it takes in and spends, so its in and out differ by its own change in balance; its details show its two printed balances from pp.186-209 and the change between them. Where pp.66-67 print more for a group than its funds' pages do, the difference sits on the same box, and the box's note says why.

caveats.text: This file holds the same money at more than one level of detail: 136 printed figures sit behind more than one link. A revenue row is behind its flow into a fund, its line's rollup into its category, and its fund's rollup into the fund's group; a spending row is behind its department's category rows and the fund-to-department link that totals them. Sum within one pair of adjacent tiers, never across the whole graph; the file publishes no headline for this reason.

Revenue and spending come from different pages and need not balance fund by fund: a fund with printed revenue and no printed spending is drawn with money arriving and none leaving, and the other way round.

caveats.summary: Each fund's own change in balance is drawn, so these can add to more than the citywide chart's.
caveats.text: Budget Book pp.186-209 print each fund's beginning and ending balance, and this chart draws the change fund by fund: 15 funds draw $7,064,200 and 17 funds contribute $6,930,000. Netted within each fund group, the same changes come to draws of $3,621,200 and contributions of $3,487,000, and that net is what the citywide chart draws, from pp.66-67's own figures. Within a fund group some funds draw and others contribute, so these add up to more than the group's net change.

caveats.summary: Transfers in and transfers out are two separate totals here, and they need not match.
caveats.text: This chart draws the money the city's funds move to one another as two totals, Transfers In and Transfers Out, without pairing each payment with its receipt; Transfers In opens into Budget Book p76's fund-by-fund list. That both total $4,510,000 does not show each payment matches a receipt; nothing here checks them against each other.

caveats.summary: Charges one city department bills another are left out of the headline totals.
caveats.text: Internal Service Funds charge other city departments for things like vehicles and computers. That is the city paying itself, so the headline leaves it out. The all-funds totals include it, and match the city's own citywide totals.

caveats.summary: The money funds hold at the start and end of the year is not drawn, only what moves.
caveats.text: Budget Book pp.66-67 print each fund group's beginning and ending working capital. Those are amounts on hand, not money moving, so the chart draws no ribbon for them, and its columns will not add up row for row to that page.

caveats.summary: The city's two Permanent Funds have no column on this page, so they are not drawn.
caveats.text: The city has a seventh kind of fund, Permanent Funds (2 funds), and Budget Book pp.66-67 print no column for them.

caveats.summary: How restricted each fund's money is comes from this site's reading of the city's fund descriptions.
caveats.text: How tightly a fund's money is restricted is this site's reading of the Description of Funds (Budget Book pp. 258-261), not a figure the city printed. Each fund shows the sentence it was read from. "unknown" means those pages do not say; it is a reading, not a gap.

caveats.summary: Every printed transfer is drawn from both ends, so adding every ribbon in this file counts each transfer twice.
caveats.text: Budget Book p76 names both ends of every transfer it prints, and this file draws both: a leg into the fund that gets the money and a leg out of the fund that sends it, under one transfer_id and at one value. So the number of transfers is half metadata.counts.links, and adding every value_cents gives twice p76's grand total: $21,525,997 in FY 2025-26 and $21,624,633 in FY 2026-27.

caveats.summary: A fund that both pays and receives appears twice, under one name.
caveats.text: This is money moving between the city's own funds, and a flow chart cannot draw a box pointing at itself. So a fund's paying end and its receiving end are separate boxes; two boxes with one name are one fund seen from both ends.

caveats.summary: Only p76's two adopted years are drawn; its two earlier columns don't add up.
caveats.text: p76's FY2023-24 and FY2024-25 columns miss its own printed grand total by $6,858,051 and by exactly $5,000,000, far more than rounding, so no figure from them is published. Budget Book pp.66-67 print no actual or revised column to check them against either.

caveats.summary: A fund's payments here are not all it transfers out: capital transfers are listed elsewhere.
caveats.text: Each receiving section of p76 equals the matching Transfers In on Budget Book pp.66-67 to the cent, so the payments drawn here add up to transfers in, not to the city's transfers out. What p76 leaves out is what each fund sends to capital projects, which p222 lists.

caveats.summary: How restricted each fund's money is comes from this site's reading of the city's fund descriptions.
caveats.text: How tightly a fund's money is restricted is this site's reading of the Description of Funds (Budget Book pp. 258-261), not a figure the city printed. Each fund shows the sentence it was read from. "unknown" means those pages do not say; it is a reading, not a gap.

caveats.summary: Every transfer out is drawn from both ends, so adding every ribbon in this file counts each twice.
caveats.text: Budget Book p76 and p222 name both ends of every transfer they print, and this file draws both, under one transfer_id and at one value. Adding every value_cents gives twice the $4,510,000 the city transfers out.

caveats.summary: The city's transfers out come from two printed lists, so a fund can appear on both.
caveats.text: Budget Book p76 lists what the operating funds transfer to one another, $4,510,000 here, and p222 what they transfer to capital project funds, $0. pp.66-67 print Transfers Out as the two together, and the build checks that sum by fund group to the cent. A fund on both lists pays both.

caveats.summary: Money sent to capital project funds leaves the citywide chart; no box there receives it.
caveats.text: Budget Book p204 prints the capital project funds on a line of their own, beside the operating budget, and pp.66-67 total the operating budget alone. So money an operating fund sends to a capital project fund leaves the citywide chart as Transfers Out. This chart draws each capital project fund that receives it, but not what that fund spends it on.

caveats.summary: A fund that both pays and receives appears twice, under one name.
caveats.text: This is money moving between the city's own funds, and a flow chart cannot draw a box pointing at itself. So a fund's paying end and its receiving end are separate boxes; two boxes with one name are one fund seen from both ends.
